name: Executive order of April 16, 1877 setting apart the Duck Valley Reservation for the Western Shoshone
nations: Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation
promises: The President withdrew a tract partly in Idaho Territory and partly in Nevada from the public domain and set it apart as a reservation for the Western Shoshone Indians, subject to boundary changes once its limits were located.
today: Royce lists this as the reserve the treaty of October 1, 1863 authorized for the Western Shoshone. No court, Indian Claims Commission or congressional finding about this order was found; the Commission's Western Shoshone dockets (326-A, 326-K) concern the Western Shoshone aboriginal lands, not this reservation.

sources.title: Rutherford B. Hayes, Executive Order Defining Duck Valley Reserve Boundaries, April 16, 1877
sources.publisher: The American Presidency Project, UC Santa Barbara

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 890

openQuestions: presentDayTribes lists the Northwestern Band of Shoshoni and the Te-Moak Tribe; the reservation set apart by this order is today held by the Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation, who are not listed.
The Shoshone-Paiute Tribes' own history page (shopaitribes.org/spculture) returned not found in this pass.
